samples.summary: New view-layer refusal→message plumbing (`refusalMessage`, `setOnNotice`, `Spreadsheet.onNotice`, sheet-view toast) has no test whatsoever
samples.evidence: The user-visible half of this change is the message text and the wiring Sheet.setOnRefusal → Worksheet.onNoticeCallback → Spreadsheet.onNotice → toast.error. Grepping the whole repo for `onNotice|setOnNotice|refusalMessage` returns only src files plus model-level `setOnRefusal` uses in tests; no test file references them. packages/sheets/test/view/ contains many Worksheet tests (worksheet-mouse, worksheet-keymap, worksheet-mobile-edit …), so this layer is testable, yet nothing asserts that a refused drag produces the string "Can't move part of a merged cell…" or that the callback fires at all. In particular `refusalMessage` maps 'merge-autofill' via a `default:` branch, so a future refusal kind would silently get the autofill text with no test to catch it.

samples.summary: Second new `consumeSpillBlocker` call site (destination merge-cover clearing in moveRangeTo) is untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds two spill-blocker consumption points in moveRangeTo: the source-clear loop (~line 2392) and the merge-covered destination clearing loop (line 2461, inside the `movedMerges` block). Only the first is exercised — calculation.test.ts:202 'spill recovers when a drag-move carries the blocking cell away' moves a single plain cell with no merges involved, so the `movedMerges.length > 0` branch containing line 2461 never runs. No test in merge.test.ts moves a merged block over a spill-blocking cell; the merge drag-move tests there assert only display strings for plain values. That branch could be deleted and the suite would stay green.
searchedFor: read new merge.test.ts drag-move tests in diff

samples.summary: 'reports nothing when there is no fill range to apply' is effectively vacuous
samples.evidence: The test builds a sheet with no merged cells and autofills a cell onto itself. autofill() returns at `if (!fillRange) return false` (sheet.ts:2565) before reaching the only `this.refuse(...)` call in the method, and even if it did reach it, `getMergesIntersecting` on a merge-free sheet can never be non-empty. So `expect(refusals).toEqual([])` holds for any plausible implementation, including a broken one — the assertion cannot fail.

samples.summary: 'should report nothing when the move goes through' asserts no refusal but never asserts the move actually happened
samples.evidence: The test moves a whole merged block A1:B1 to row 3 and only asserts `refusals` is empty. It makes no assertion about cell contents or merge location at the destination, so a regression where moveRangeTo silently returns early (or drops the merge) without calling refuse() would still pass, and the test would report 'the move goes through' when it did not. Adding a toDisplayString/merge-location assertion would make the negative case meaningful.

finding.summary: New view-layer refusal→message plumbing (`refusalMessage`, `setOnNotice`, `Spreadsheet.onNotice`, sheet-view toast) has no test whatsoever
finding.evidence: The user-visible half of this change is the message text and the wiring Sheet.setOnRefusal → Worksheet.onNoticeCallback → Spreadsheet.onNotice → toast.error. Grepping the whole repo for `onNotice|setOnNotice|refusalMessage` returns only src files plus model-level `setOnRefusal` uses in tests; no test file references them. packages/sheets/test/view/ contains many Worksheet tests (worksheet-mouse, worksheet-keymap, worksheet-mobile-edit …), so this layer is testable, yet nothing asserts that a refused drag produces the string "Can't move part of a merged cell…" or that the callback fires at all. In particular `refusalMessage` maps 'merge-autofill' via a `default:` branch, so a future refusal kind would silently get the autofill text with no test to catch it.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `refusalMessage` (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:98-110), the `setOnRefusal`→`onNoticeCallback` wiring (worksheet.ts:417-419), `setOnNotice` (worksheet.ts:855-857), `Spreadsheet.onNotice` (spreadsheet.ts:414-416) and the host toast (sheet-view.tsx:1018-1022) exist, but no test anywhere exercises them. Repo-wide greps for the identifiers return only src files plus model-level `Sheet.setOnRefusal` tests (merge.test.ts:266,288,309; autofill.test.ts:211,227) which assert refusal *kinds*, never the message text or the view callback. Greps for the user-visible strings ("Can't move part of a merged cell", "merged cell") match no test file containing the notice text; co-located src tests (src/view/__tests__/*), packages/frontend/src and packages/frontend/tests, and the absence of any e2e suite were all checked. The only related harness artifact is a screenshot scenario about merge rendering (sheet-scenarios.tsx:633-637), with no notice assertion. The layer is demonstrably testable — worksheet-mouse.test.ts:26-59 drives Worksheet.prototype methods directly. So a user-visible behavior change ships with zero coverage, including the permissive `default:` branch that would silently return autofill text for any future refusal kind. In-lane (missing tests) and blocking.

finding.summary: Second new `consumeSpillBlocker` call site (destination merge-cover clearing in moveRangeTo) is untested
finding.evidence: The diff adds two spill-blocker consumption points in moveRangeTo: the source-clear loop (~line 2392) and the merge-covered destination clearing loop (line 2461, inside the `movedMerges` block). Only the first is exercised — calculation.test.ts:202 'spill recovers when a drag-move carries the blocking cell away' moves a single plain cell with no merges involved, so the `movedMerges.length > 0` branch containing line 2461 never runs. No test in merge.test.ts moves a merged block over a spill-blocking cell; the merge drag-move tests there assert only display strings for plain values. That branch could be deleted and the suite would stay green.
searchedFor: read new merge.test.ts drag-move tests in diff

verdict.reason: The second `consumeSpillBlocker` call site in `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2461, inside the `movedMerges` destination merge-cover clearing loop) has no test that can exercise it. Repo-wide grep shows only two test files invoke `moveRangeTo`: calculation.test.ts:212 and merge.test.ts (11 call sites). calculation.test.ts:202-225 moves a single plain cell A5→D8 with no merges, so `movedMerges` is empty and the entire 2404-2466 block is skipped. merge.test.ts contains zero occurrences of `spill` and none of the spill-producing functions (MINVERSE/MMULT/TRANSPOSE/MUNIT/SEQUENCE); its move tests use plain scalars ('10','20','ghost','7'). merge.test.ts:192-213 does enter the 2429-2463 loop, but with a plain 'ghost' cell — no entry ever exists in `spillBlockers`, so line 2461 returns undefined and the call could be deleted with the suite still green. Cross-checks for other entry points (mergeSelection in pivot-protection.test.ts and data-validation.test.ts; the sole production caller view/worksheet.ts:4340) turned up no test that moves a merged block over a spill-blocking cell. No counterexample exists; the branch is genuinely untested.
